title: Truncation resolves the augmentation kernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring in universe $u$, $M$ an object of $\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{v}(R)$, $n\in\mathbf N$, and $P$ a projective resolution of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Suppose $P_i$ is a zero object for every $i>n+1$. Then the kernel of the augmentation $P_0\to M$ admits a projective resolution of length at most $n$ in the same module universe $v$. No relation between $u$ and $v$ and no enough-projectives hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension), successor proof, and Lemma 065S (1): use the supplied resolution itself

proof.text: Set K = ChainComplex.truncate.obj P.complex. Its degree i is P_(i+1). Factor the old differential P_1 → P_0 through the augmentation kernel using kernel.lift and P.complex_d_comp_π_f_zero. P.exact₀.epi_kernelLift makes the factorization an epimorphism.

The new augmentation kills K.d 1 0: compose with the monic kernel inclusion and use P.complex.d_comp_d. A short-complex morphism with identity first and second components and the kernel inclusion third component transfers exactness from P.exact_succ 0 using ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono.

Use ChainComplex.toSingle₀Equiv to package the augmentation. At degree zero the quasi-isomorphism condition is its exactness and epimorphism; at positive degrees it is P.exact_succ with indices shifted. The terms are projective by P.projective. The vanishing bound follows from n<i implying n+1<i+1.

    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : ModuleCat.{v} R} (n : ℕ)
